assumptions.condition: There exists a strict total order \(\succ_g\) on \(\mathcal B\) such that \(g(z)\) is the \(\succ_g\)-maximal element of \(\{d\in\mathcal B:d\subseteq z\}\) for every \(z\in\mathcal B\).

standard.name: WARP rationalization on finite nested menus

novel.justification: The comparison class retains every population generated by independently responsive subsets of the three offered factors. These eight maps are the one-sided specialization of the standard coordinate-specific receipt model used by factorial-IV analyses, so requiring their inclusion prevents maximality from being manufactured by deleting ordinary compliance patterns.

assumptions.condition: \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent and identically distributed according to \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\).
For every \(t\in\mathcal B\) and fixed \(u\in\mathbb R\), \(\operatorname{Var}_P(\phi_{m,t}-u\phi_{p,t})>0\).

definitions.name: WARP-rational one-sided response class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal G^{\mathrm{WARP}}_3=\{g\in\mathfrak G_3: g(z)\subseteq z\ \forall z\in\mathcal B\text{ and }\exists\succ_g\text{ a strict total order with }g(z)=\max_{\succ_g}\{d\in\mathcal B:d\subseteq z\}\ \forall z\in\mathcal B\}\).

definitions.name: Möbius-null envelope
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal N_3=\{g\in\mathcal G^{\mathrm{WARP}}_3:\sigma_t(g)=0\ \forall t\in\mathcal B\}\) and \(\mathcal E_3=\{g^\star\}\cup\mathcal N_3\).

definitions.name: Four symbolic null families
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal F_3\) is the set of maps of the following four disjoint forms, where \(a,b,c\) are distinct elements of \(U\): (i) \(g(z)=\varnothing\); (ii) for \(s\in\{\varnothing,\{b\},\{c\}\}\), choose \(\{a\}\) whenever \(a\in z\), otherwise choose \(s\) whenever \(s\ne\varnothing\) and \(s\subseteq z\), and otherwise choose \(\varnothing\); (iii) for an unordered pair \(\{a,b\}\) and \((\rho_a,\rho_b)\in\{0,1\}^2\), choose \(\{a,b\}\) when \(\{a,b\}\subseteq z\), otherwise choose \(\{a\}\) if \(a\in z\) and \(\rho_a=1\), otherwise choose \(\{b\}\) if \(b\in z\) and \(\rho_b=1\), and otherwise choose \(\varnothing\); (iv) for an unordered pair \(\{a,b\}\) with remaining factor \(c\), either choose by the priority \(\{a,b\}\succ\{b\}\succ\{c\}\succ\varnothing\) with \(\{a\}\) below \(\varnothing\), or symmetrically by \(\{a,b\}\succ\{a\}\succ\{c\}\succ\varnothing\) with \(\{b\}\) below \(\varnothing\), placing every unlisted bundle below \(\varnothing\).

definitions.name: Outcome-nonrestrictive identification on \(\mathcal M\)
definitions.construction: The vector \((\mu_t^\star)_{t\in\mathcal B}\) is outcome-nonrestrictively identified on \(\mathcal M\) when any two laws satisfying the maintained assumptions, supported on \(\mathcal M\), having \(p^\star>0\), and inducing the same \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\), have the same vector \((\mu_t^\star)_{t\in\mathcal B}\), without any further restriction on the conditional law of \((Y(t))_{t\in\mathcal B}\) given \(G\).

definitions.name: Contraction--Möbius classification handle
definitions.construction: Start from contraction consistency \(g(z)=r\) and \(r\subseteq w\subseteq z\Rightarrow g(w)=r\); condition on the full-offer choice \(g(U)\); reduce \(\sigma_t(g)=0\) first at triples, then pairs, then singletons; and close each branch by an explicit strict ranking. The target object is a non-enumerative proof that the full-offer-pair branch has exactly four maps with the remaining factor unresponsive and two with it responsive.

definitions.name: Perfect-complier Walsh contrasts
definitions.construction: \(\chi_S(t)=\prod_{j\in S}(2\mathbf 1\{j\in t\}-1)\), \(H_{S,t}=2^{-2}\chi_S(t)\), and \(\theta_S=2^{-2}\sum_{t\in\mathcal B}\chi_S(t)\mu_t^\star\) for every nonempty \(S\subseteq U\).

definitions.name: Subset-inversion observational-null construction
definitions.construction: For \(h\in\mathcal G^{\mathrm{WARP}}_3\setminus\mathcal E_3\), select \(t\) with \(\sigma_t(h)\ne0\), set \(V=U\setminus t\), \(v_h(S)=\mathbf 1\{h(t\cup S)=t\}\), \(\beta_{t\cup B_0}=\sum_{Q\subseteq B_0}(-1)^{|B_0|-|Q|}v_h(V\setminus Q)\), \(n_h=1\), and \(n_{g_{C_0}}=-\beta_{C_0}\) for \(C_0\supseteq t\), with all remaining \(n_g=0\). Under both \(P_+\) and \(P_-\), assign mass \(q_g=1/9\) to each of the eight maps \(g_{C_0}\) and to \(h\); choose \(\varepsilon=(36\max_g|n_g|)^{-1}\); set \(P_\pm(Y(s)=1\mid G=g)=1/2\) for \(s\ne t\) and \(P_\pm(Y(t)=1\mid G=g)=1/2\pm\varepsilon n_g/q_g\), with the potential outcomes conditionally mutually independent.

definitions.name: Signed-ratio and Walsh estimators
definitions.construction: Let \(\widehat q_{zt}\) and \(\widehat r_{zt}\) be the within-\(Z=z\) sample means of \(\mathbf 1\{D=t\}\) and \(Y\mathbf 1\{D=t\}\). Set \(\widehat p_t=\sum_{z\supseteq t}(-1)^{|z|-|t|}\widehat q_{zt}\), \(\widehat m_t=\sum_{z\supseteq t}(-1)^{|z|-|t|}\widehat r_{zt}\), \(\widehat\mu_t=\widehat m_t/\widehat p_t\), and \(\widehat{\boldsymbol\theta}=H(\widehat\mu_t)_{t\in\mathcal B}\).

definitions.name: Bonferroni--Fieller inversion
definitions.construction: For each \(t\in\mathcal B\), \(\mathcal F_t=\{u\in\mathbb R:n(\widehat m_t-u\widehat p_t)^2\le z_{1-\alpha_0/16}^2\widehat{\operatorname{Var}}(\phi_{m,t}-u\phi_{p,t})\}\); the simultaneous Walsh region is \(H(\prod_{t\in\mathcal B}\mathcal F_t)\).

statements.statement: Can the contraction--Möbius handle establish \(\mathcal N_3=\mathcal F_3\) without enumerating response maps, including a proof that when \(g(U)=\{a,b\}\) the remaining factor \(c\) yields exactly four null maps when unresponsive alone and exactly two null maps when responsive alone?
statements.justification: This is the non-enumerative behavioral step that turns a finite search result into an economic choice theorem.
statements.gap: Goff's two-factor application uses exhaustive search and does not resolve the first three-factor full-offer-pair branch.
statements.consumer: A solution certifies the response class used by Theorems 1--3 and makes the resulting relaxation auditable without code.

statements.statement: Fix \(t\in\mathcal B\). If \(\lambda_t(z)=0\) for \(z\not\supseteq t\) and \(\sum_{z\in\mathcal B}\lambda_t(z)\mathbf 1\{g_{C_0}(z)=t\}=\mathbf 1\{C_0=U\}\) for every \(C_0\subseteq U\), then uniquely \(\lambda_t(z)=a_t(z)\) for every \(z\in\mathcal B\).
statements.justification: The separable benchmark itself forces the Boolean Möbius weights, so the envelope is not chosen to fit a desired answer.
statements.gap: The generic row-space criterion does not explain why these coefficients are unique once every coordinate-separable type is retained.
statements.consumer: The lemma fixes the only candidate observable recovery map and reduces maximality to a transparent signature test.

statements.statement: The Möbius-null WARP set satisfies \(\mathcal N_3=\mathcal F_3\). Its four disjoint families have cardinalities \(1\), \(9\), \(12\), and \(6\), respectively. Hence \(|\mathcal N_3|=28\), \(|\mathcal E_3|=29\), exactly eight elements of \(\mathcal E_3\) are coordinate-separable, exactly 21 are interactive, and exactly six maps \(g\in\mathcal N_3\) satisfy \(I(g)=\varnothing\).
statements.justification: The exact count and the six fully interactive maps show that the admissible relaxation is substantively larger than coordinate-specific receipt.
statements.gap: No inspected paper gives a symbolic three-factor WARP classification subject to simultaneous zero-Möbius restrictions.
statements.consumer: The theorem provides a finite, interpretable compliance menu for \(\texttt{factiv::iv\_factorial}\) users and the New Haven factorial-IV analysis.

statements.statement: For every \(\mathcal M\subseteq\mathcal G^{\mathrm{WARP}}_3\) with \(\mathcal S_3\subseteq\mathcal M\), the vector \((\mu_t^\star)_{t\in\mathcal B}\) is outcome-nonrestrictively identified on \(\mathcal M\) if and only if \(\mathcal M\subseteq\mathcal E_3\). Consequently \(\mathcal E_3\) is the unique inclusion-maximal such support. Relative to the coordinate-separable support \(\mathcal S_3\) of Blackwell and Pashley, this strictly enlarges the admissible response family from eight to 29 maps while preserving the same eight perfect-complier means.
statements.justification: The iff statement identifies the largest economically rational relaxation rather than offering another sufficient compliance restriction.
statements.gap: Blackwell--Pashley impose coordinate-specific receipt, while Goff supplies a generic criterion and a two-factor boundary rather than this three-factor maximal support.
statements.consumer: The theorem tells factorial-IV analysts exactly which interactive uptake behaviors leave every perfect-complier factorial estimand intact.

statements.statement: If \(\mathcal M\subseteq\mathcal E_3\), then for every \(t\in\mathcal B\), \(p_t=p^\star\), \(m_t=p^\star\mu_t^\star\), and \(\mu_t^\star=m_t/p_t\). Therefore every nonempty perfect-complier factorial effect is identified by \(\theta_S=2^{-2}\sum_{t\in\mathcal B}\chi_S(t)m_t/p_t\).
statements.justification: The formulas translate the behavioral envelope into estimands computable from randomized assignment cells.
statements.gap: The signed ratios coincide algebraically with existing perfect-complier formulas under separable receipt; the new claim is their validity on the strictly larger classified envelope.
statements.consumer: The result directly supplies all seven main and interaction effects required by a three-factor perfect-complier analysis.

statements.statement: For every \(h\in\mathcal G^{\mathrm{WARP}}_3\setminus\mathcal E_3\), there exist two finite laws \(P_+\) and \(P_-\), supported on \(\mathcal S_3\cup\{h\}\), with full-support randomized \(Z\), common positive response-type masses, and mutually independent Bernoulli potential outcomes conditional on type, such that \(\mathcal L_{P_+}(Z,D,Y)=\mathcal L_{P_-}(Z,D,Y)\) but \(\mu_t^\star(P_+)\ne\mu_t^\star(P_-)\) for at least one \(t\). The construction may keep every Bernoulli probability in \([1/4,3/4]\).
statements.justification: Complete equality of the observed law rules out reliance on a failed diagnostic moment and certifies outcome-nonrestrictive maximality.
statements.gap: Goff's row-space converse implies nonidentification abstractly; the proposed subset-inversion witness is explicit for every excluded rational addition and preserves nondegenerate Bernoulli outcomes.
statements.consumer: The countermodels prevent researchers from interpreting signed ratios after adding any behavior outside the envelope, even when first-stage diagnostics happen to cancel.

statements.statement: Under i.i.d. sampling, finite second moments, \(p^\star\ge\kappa>0\), and positive definite \(\Omega\), \(\sqrt n(\widehat{\boldsymbol\theta}-\boldsymbol\theta)=n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_{\theta}(O_i)+o_P(1)\Rightarrow N(0,\Omega)\). The plug-in \(\widehat\Omega\) is consistent and \(P(\boldsymbol\theta\in\mathcal C_{\theta})\to1-\alpha_0\).
statements.justification: All effects share signed cell moments and denominators, so joint covariance propagation is necessary for simultaneous claims.
statements.gap: Blackwell--Pashley provide the scalar and vector factorial-IV ingredients; this theorem records their adaptation to the Möbius vector and is an inference rung rather than the novelty kernel.
statements.consumer: The result permits family-wise statements about all seven factorial effects in software and applied reanalysis when the perfect-complier share is not weak.

statements.statement: Under i.i.d. sampling, finite second moments, full assignment support, and Fieller nondegeneracy, \(P\bigl((\mu_t^\star)_{t\in\mathcal B}\in\prod_{t\in\mathcal B}\mathcal F_t\bigr)\ge1-\alpha_0+o(1)\). Hence \(H(\prod_{t\in\mathcal B}\mathcal F_t)\) covers \(\boldsymbol\theta\) with probability at least \(1-\alpha_0+o(1)\); the set may be unbounded or disconnected.
statements.justification: Test inversion remains informative about identification weakness because it is allowed to return unbounded sets.
statements.gap: Existing factorial-IV work treats scalar Fieller intervals; the contribution here is the explicit Bonferroni product and Walsh image for the dependent eight-ratio system, not uniform weak-share adaptation.
statements.consumer: Applied analysts obtain a simultaneous fallback when the estimated perfect-complier share is too small for the Wald ellipsoid.

sampling_model.design: Full-support randomized assignment \(Z\in2^{\{A,B,C\}}\) with known or consistently estimated arm probabilities \(\pi_z\).
sampling_model.units: The identification model is superpopulation-based; the inference result uses i.i.d. draws \(O_i=(Z_i,D_i,Y_i)\).
sampling_model.treatment: One-sided WARP-rational received bundles satisfy \(D_i=G_i(Z_i)\subseteq Z_i\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every assignment arm has positive probability; Wald inference additionally requires \(p^\star\ge\kappa>0\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Estimate the 27 feasible receipt probabilities and 27 corresponding outcome moments by within-arm sample means, then apply the fixed Möbius and Walsh maps.

estimand_functional: \(\mu_t^\star=\dfrac{\sum_{z\supseteq t}(-1)^{|z|-|t|}\,\mathbb E_P[Y\mathbf 1\{D=t\}\mid Z=z]}{\sum_{z\supseteq t}(-1)^{|z|-|t|}\,P(D=t\mid Z=z)},\quad \boldsymbol\theta=H(\mu_t^\star)_{t\in\mathcal B}\)

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The perfect-complier average factorial effect is \(\bar\gamma_j=\bar\tau_{j,p}/\bar\delta_{L-1}\).
Unordered monotonicity implies and is implied by additive separability of choice equations in observed and unobserved variables.
Certain causal parameters are identified if and only if a version of the kappa of Abadie exists.
If treatment takeup is driven by both instruments, it becomes difficult to separate treatment interaction from treatment effect heterogeneity.
The paper derives partial-identification bounds on complier average factorial effects under milder noncompliance assumptions.
The paper provides nonparametric estimators and derives their finite-population distributions as sample size increases.
Exact and almost-exact randomization inference yields confidence sets that can be unbounded under weak compliance.

tldr: A randomized three-factor offer design can tolerate economically meaningful interactive compliance without restricting outcome heterogeneity. The proposed kernel characterizes the unique largest WARP-rational response support containing every coordinate-separable response map for which all eight perfect-complier potential-outcome means remain identified. The class is the union of the perfect-complier map and the WARP maps with zero Boolean Möbius signatures; a symbolic choice argument must show that it contains exactly 29 maps, including 21 interactive maps and six maps for which every offer coordinate matters. Signed assignment-cell transforms identify the eight means, Walsh transforms identify all seven factorial effects, and an explicit Bernoulli null-space construction proves failure after any excluded rational type is added. Joint influence functions yield simultaneous Wald inference away from a zero perfect-complier share, while Bonferroni--Fieller inversion remains honest about weak denominators.

project_justification.gap: Goff's finite-support criterion characterizes outcome-nonrestrictive identification abstractly and gives a two-factor WARP application, while Blackwell and Pashley identify arbitrary-factor perfect-complier effects by imposing coordinate-specific receipt. Neither accessible result supplies a symbolic three-factor WARP envelope that is simultaneously sufficient and maximal for the entire vector of perfect-complier means.
project_justification.niche: Three factors are the first Boolean lattice on which rational, one-sided uptake admits null-signature maps that are interactive in every assignment coordinate. This creates a sharp behavioral boundary that is invisible in the two-factor result and excluded by coordinate-specific treatment receipt.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the Möbius coefficients from the separable baseline, classifies every WARP map annihilated by those coefficients, proves the identifying formulas, and constructs observationally equivalent Bernoulli laws for every forbidden enlargement. The inference rung propagates the common signed denominator through all eight means and seven Walsh contrasts without claiming uniform adaptation as the denominator vanishes.

related_work: Goff's Theorems 1--2 provide the finite-support outcome-nonrestrictive row-space criterion that informs the algebraic endpoint here; the present theorem does not claim to improve that generic criterion. Blackwell and Pashley's perfect-complier construction identifies the same factorial targets under coordinate-specific treatment receipt; Theorem 2 strictly enlarges that behavioral support in the one-sided three-factor model. Heckman and Pinto connect rational discrete choice to binary response matrices, which informs the contraction and incidence-matrix proof strategy but does not impose the proposed simultaneous Möbius-null equations. Navjeevan, Pinto, and Santos give an operator-range and generalized-kappa characterization for latent moments, against which the signed recovery functional can be checked. Kormos, Lieli, and Huber show that coordinated two-factor takeup generally mixes causal interaction and heterogeneity, motivating an exact positive class rather than an unrestricted interpretation. Blackwell and Pashley's later bounds paper shows how weaker factorial receipt assumptions typically move the problem to partial identification. Picchetti supplies a current finite-population inference benchmark under factor-specific uptake, while Kang, Peck, and Keele provide the weak-IV inversion logic adapted in the final inference statement.
technical_internal_limitation: The separate supplemental material C to Blackwell and Pashley (2023) was not retrievable through the publisher, author page, indexed web results, Crossref metadata, or the accessible 13-page author PDF. The main article describes that supplement as giving a more complicated weighted interpretation under weaker treatment exclusion and says interactions become less clear; it does not expose a maximal three-factor perfect-complier support theorem. Novelty remains conditional on an external audit confirming that supplement C does not admit the six null maps with \(I(g)=\varnothing\) and state an equivalent 29-map envelope. A second diagnostic is internal: equality of the eight probability transforms alone does not certify \(\mathcal M\subseteq\mathcal E_3\), because mixtures of excluded types can cancel their signatures while type-specific outcome moments do not cancel.
honest_scope: The open mathematical content is the non-enumerative equality \(\mathcal N_3=\mathcal F_3\), especially the full-offer-pair branch, and the explicit all-additions converse. The row-space criterion, Boolean inversion identity, signed-ratio estimation, multivariate delta method, Wald ellipsoid, and Fieller inversion are established techniques adapted to the classified support. Replacing \(U\) by any two-element factor set collapses the null envelope to the empty map and the two single-factor separable maps; after adding the perfect map, this recovers Goff's four-type two-factor boundary. The proposal does not cover two-sided receipt, missing assignment arms, arbitrary \(K\), classes that omit separable types, rank-adaptive singular Wald inference, or uniform coverage along sequences with \(p_n^\star\to0\).

seed_details.anchor_receipt: The arXiv source was opened at the Introduction, Theorems 1--2, Proposition 4, its proof discussion, and the Conclusion. The paper proves a finite-support row-space criterion and uses exhaustive search for a two-factor WARP complementarity model; its conclusion explicitly notes rapid computational scaling.
seed_details.question: Is the unique inclusion-maximal WARP support containing every coordinate-separable map and identifying all eight three-factor perfect-complier means exactly \(\mathcal E_3=\{g^\star\}\cup\{g:\sigma_t(g)=0\ \forall t\}\), and does it contain exactly 29 maps?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace Goff's enumeration of binary collections by a symbolic contraction-consistency analysis of WARP choice on the Boolean lattice; the unresolved branch is \(g(U)=\{a,b\}\), where the singleton Möbius equations must force exactly four maps with \(c\) unresponsive and two with \(c\) responsive.
seed_details.destination_search: Exact searches for three-factor perfect compliers combined with WARP, interactive compliance, response maps, and Möbius inversion returned no competing classification; the current 2025--2026 adjacent papers retain coordinate-specific uptake or generic operator criteria.
seed_details.referee_objection: Immediate from Goff because his necessary-and-sufficient row-space theorem can enumerate any finite selection model.
seed_details.rebuttal: The row-space theorem supplies the algebraic test but neither the WARP-to-Möbius equivalence nor the non-enumerative 29-map behavioral classification; the full-offer-pair branch is a new revealed-preference theorem.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: The arXiv source was opened at Proposition 4 and the associated row-space intersection for a contrast-valued target. It establishes parameter-specific identification for a two-factor interaction without first identifying every latent mean.
seed_details.question: For each nonempty \(S\subseteq U\), what are all inclusion-maximal WARP supports identifying only the perfect-complier Walsh effect \(\theta_S\), including supports on which some component means are not identified?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the intersection of eight mean-specific row spaces by the single contrast-weighted row-space condition and solve its WARP-compatible maximal supports.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches pairing three-factor Walsh contrasts with WARP compliance found factorial estimands under treatment exclusion and two-factor interaction analyses, but no seven-contrast support classification.
seed_details.referee_objection: This is a mechanical rerun of Goff's parameter-specific brute-force algorithm for seven fixed vectors.
seed_details.rebuttal: A publishable version requires symbolic orbit representatives and exact maximality certificates for every Walsh order; mere enumeration would not survive the objection.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: The arXiv source was opened at the Introduction, the restricted design-matrix results, and the Discussion. It derives aliasing and variance results for fractional or incomplete factorial assignment effects, not endogenous receipt.
seed_details.question: For an arbitrary observed offer subset \(\mathcal Z_0\subseteq\mathcal B\), which perfect-complier means and Walsh effects are identified under WARP, and what minimum arm augmentation restores each target?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace full Boolean Möbius inversion by the restricted treatment-incidence operator on \(\mathcal Z_0\) and characterize target row-space membership uniformly over WARP types.
seed_details.destination_search: The target--method search found incomplete factorial aliasing without noncompliance and finite-IV row-space criteria with full factorial offers, but no WARP receipt criterion for missing offer cells.
seed_details.referee_objection: This is ordinary fractional-factorial aliasing with a larger design matrix.
seed_details.rebuttal: Endogenous bundle choice couples all missing-arm restrictions through a single rational response map, so ordinary contrast aliasing is neither sufficient nor necessary for local perfect-complier identification.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: The Introduction and Conclusion of the arXiv source were opened together with the exhaustive finite-support algorithm. The paper explicitly identifies computational scaling as a limitation and does not give an arbitrary-factor rational-choice count.
seed_details.question: For arbitrary \(K\), can WARP maps with all Boolean Möbius signatures equal to zero be characterized recursively and counted without enumerating all response maps?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Lift the three-factor contraction branches to principal ideals of \(2^{[K]}\) and prove compatibility of the local recursions across overlapping ideals.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches combining Boolean-lattice Möbius inversion, WARP response maps, and factorial noncompliance did not locate a recurrence or exact count.
seed_details.referee_objection: The arbitrary-\(K\) statement is an aspirational combinatorics program with no credible recurrence.
seed_details.rebuttal: The three-factor identities expose a possible recursion, but no closed induction invariant was verified, so this seed is not selected for the current version.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: The arXiv source was opened at the Introduction, Propositions 1--2, the two-factor sharp-bound supplement, and its final remarks. It gives analytic constant-complier bounds for general \(K\) and an LP sharpness calculation for binary outcomes with two factors.
seed_details.question: Over the full three-factor WARP response polytope with bounded outcomes, are the sharp identified sets for perfect-complier means and Walsh effects the optima of an explicit finite linear-fractional program, and which effects admit closed-form facets?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace factorwise conditional-complier strata by all 244 WARP response maps and couple type probabilities to eight bundle-specific bounded outcome moments before optimizing a common perfect-complier ratio.
seed_details.destination_search: The destination search found two-factor factorial bounds and generic latent-type programs, but not a three-factor WARP-compatible sharp region for perfect compliers.
seed_details.referee_objection: Once the 244 types are listed, Balke--Pearl linear programming makes the result automatic.
seed_details.rebuttal: A generic program alone would be too thin; explicit facets or a dual support-function theorem plus uniform endpoint inference would be required, which exceeds the fixed exact-identification angle.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: The testing subsection and empirical WARP application were opened. Goff derives nonnegativity and equality restrictions from binary combinations and uses them to assess a two-factor selection model.
seed_details.question: What is the irredundant facet description of the observable first-stage polytope generated by \(\mathcal E_3\), and which outcome-distribution inequalities distinguish it from mixtures outside the envelope that pass all eight probability transforms?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Project the 29-type incidence simplex into the 27 feasible assignment--receipt probabilities and compute a symbolic facet orbit decomposition before adding outcome-distribution inequalities.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for testable implications of three-factor WARP noncompliance found only generic finite-mixture and two-factor binary-combination restrictions.
seed_details.referee_objection: This is polyhedral bookkeeping and does not identify a causal estimand.
seed_details.rebuttal: The probability diagnostics are provably insufficient, but the proposed outcome-distribution facets would be useful only as a companion result rather than the paper's kernel.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: The author PDF was opened at Sections 2.4, 3.2--3.3, and the conclusion. It derives perfect-complier ratios, finite-population and superpopulation limits, and scalar Fieller inversion under coordinate-specific receipt.
seed_details.question: Can the eight dependent signed ratios and seven Walsh transforms be given a joint influence-function representation, simultaneous Wald coverage away from zero compliance, and simultaneous Fieller inversion under a weak common denominator?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Stack all signed assignment-cell outcome and receipt moments before ratio linearization; the common denominator and Walsh map create dependence absent from scalar intervals.
seed_details.destination_search: Picchetti's 2026 finite-population paper and Blackwell--Pashley supply nearby vector CLTs and scalar inversion, but the exact Möbius vector is not treated.
seed_details.referee_objection: This follows immediately from a multivariate CLT, delta method, and Bonferroni.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds for fixed positive shares; this is retained only as an inference rung and not presented as the novel kernel.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: The paper was opened at the Introduction, Theorem 3, the decomposition proof, and the subsequent partial-identification section. It shows in a two-factor design how saturated IV interactions mix causal interaction with heterogeneity components under coordinated takeup.
seed_details.question: For three factors, can the conventional saturated-IV three-way interaction be decomposed into the perfect-complier Walsh interaction and design-computable weights on coordinated-compliance heterogeneity terms, with an exact zero-distortion condition?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Expand the saturated instrument basis over three-factor response types and collect the actual estimand by WARP orbits before characterizing when every contamination weight vanishes.
